newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Cargo to leave IATA tariff conference.
newsitem.headline: KLM Cargo to leave IATA tariff conference.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday its cargo unit planned to pull out of the IATA tariff conference at the end of 1997.

"In the eyes of KLM Cargo it's not beneficial towards the industry to make that kind of agreement because it has no value in practice. It's already the case that tariffs are decided by the companies themselves," a spokesman said.
The International Air Transport Association (IATA), which groups the worlds major airlines, has a framework for setting suggested cargo rates for its members.
"It is KLM's opinion that it is not justified to continue with that kind of negotiation," the spokesman said.

He said KLM Cargo was planning to pull out of the tariff conference by December 31, but added KLM wanted to remain an active member of IATA. "Numerous activities of IATA are very, very worthwhile but the tariff conference we don't see the need for," the spokesman said.
